headline: Transformer and deep learning tools benchmarked against established genomics methods
label: Benchmarking Computational Biology Models
summary: Recent preprints and papers benchmark transformer and deep learning models for long-read taxonomy, gene prediction, and proteomics against established tools.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of deep learning models against established baselines across genomic and proteomic tasks. Metaxa compares against Kraken 2 and MetageNN on long Nanopore reads, with genus-level gains on out-of-sample taxa. Tiberius is extended to lineage-specific ab initio gene models across six eukaryotic clades and benchmarked on 33 species, while OrionGeno reports outperformance over existing annotation methods. DDA-BERT improves peptide identification over existing rescoring tools, and metagenomic-deepFRI adds structural templates to protein function annotation. OGR pairs a 1.25B-parameter MoE foundation model trained on 422 rice genomes with an open benchmark suite. Not every item shares this emphasis: TaxVAMB addresses metagenome binning through a semisupervised variational autoencoder. What distinguishes this set is explicit testing of generalization across clades, out-of-sample taxa, and species, alongside released benchmark infrastructure.
